panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Upright whole-spine AP radiograph of the 19-year-old sister in a familial lumbar Scheuermann disease report. Qualifying Scheuermann manifestation (vertebral wedging at L1–L3) is attributed in-text to these whole-spine radiographs; the panel-specific captioned value is a coronal Cobb angle, so confidence is moderate. [raw subtype: lumbar] B: Upright lateral (sagittal) whole-spine radiograph of the same sister showing the lumbar Scheuermann manifestation: anterior vertebral wedging at L1–L3 with a localized/angular kyphotic angulation of 37°. Lumbar (rather than classic thoracic) localization is a recognized variant. [raw subtype: lumbar]

in_text_mentions: at L2 to L3 with localized kyphotic angulation of 70°, and a coronal Cobb angle of 20° at L1 to L5; there was slight displacement and instability of the lumbar vertebra; and there was a diagnosis of degenerative scoliosis (Fig. 2). The proband's 19-year-old sister did not show kyphotic deformity, pain, or dysfunction of the lower back; in addition, there were no positive neurological signs. Radiographs of the F-S-AP and LAT x-ray showed a “wedging” shape of the vertebrae at L1 to L3, a localized kyphotic angulation of 37°, and a Cobb angle of 15° at T9 to T12, with a diagnosis of IS (Fig. 3).
